findings: Both original PDS4 raw products declare the 51-byte housekeeping array at byte2148480. Big-endian decoding yields48 scalar values and12 flag values matching corresponding numeric FITS header fields across the two files.

The document calls its first ULON field MET_IMG. Stored values35398318/35398319 match FITS MET_HK, while image MET is35398319/35398320. This correspondence is not a one-second timing correction or independently established flight-software semantics.

The byte49 MSB-first interpretation TEMPCVRT,CLMP2PE,CLMP1PE,SOURCE,FORMAT,EXPMODE matches the headers. This two-product correspondence does not establish general bit order, software-version identity or physical operating state.

LVPS/FPU values are uncalibrated stored integers; voltage/current/temperature descriptions are not conversion functions. EXPOSURE40 matches the header, with document units1ms; no timing-erratum application or effective-exposure recalibration.

All210 fixed-width records are339 bytes including CRLF, matching label and71190-byte table. Generic CSV parsing differs in rows56 and202 because description text contains unescaped quotations. Declared fixed-width fields and original bytes are retained without repair.

Four ELARA planning rows80/148/188/204 are present. Row204 JELO_LPHASE04 and row203 LPHASE04 share printed2007-03-05T11:00:00 and1/0035398317:30519; the description says placeholder details not yet worked out. Next distinct start March6 is Himalia, not Elara.

The sequence label expressly says its intended sequence list was not validated against actual spacecraft activities and presence does not guarantee observations. Duplicate start rows prevent naive per-row positive duration inference. Planning proximity is not independent product/target/pointing identification.
